content: Aluminium fluoride (AlF₃) is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula AlF₃. It can be synthesized by reacting aluminium hydroxide or metallic aluminium with hydrogen fluoride (HF). In its solid state, the structure of aluminium fluoride resembles that of rhenium trioxide (ReO₃), consisting of distorted AlF₆ octahedra. Aluminium fluoride is highly refractory, which is in stark contrast to other aluminium halides such as aluminium chloride (AlCl₃), aluminium bromide (AlBr₃), and aluminium iodide (AlI₃). These other halides are dimeric in their liquid state and also evaporate as dimers. In the gas phase, at approximately 1000°C, aluminium fluoride exists as trigonal molecules with D₃h symmetry. The bond lengths between aluminium and fluorine in this state are measured to be 163 pm. Aluminium fluoride plays a critical role as an additive in the electrolytic production of aluminium. It is used to lower the melting point of the alumina feedstock and to enhance the conductivity of the electrolyte, thereby improving the efficiency of the process.
